battle.name: 英藏戰爭
battle.brief: 1903年英藏戰爭中，英國遠征軍由印度進入西藏，於昌都一帶與藏軍交鋒。英軍野戰部隊配備德製婆塞德後膛砲（Breech-loading cannon，1870年），以其射速與曲射能力提供前線支援，協助占據昌都；戰事其後向拉薩方向延伸，並於1904年迫使藏方議和。

kit.name: 婆塞德後膛砲
kit.history: 婆塞德後膛砲是德國陸軍炮兵體系的重型後膛火砲，主要隸屬野戰炮兵，負責提供間接曲射火力，並在部隊推進、守備與攻堅時支援步兵作戰。

countries: 這場戰爭於1903年12月由英屬印度越過錫金與西藏間的杰萊普山口（Jelep La），軍事行動延續到1904年，因此較準確的名稱是1903至1904年第一次英藏戰役。英方交戰主體為大不列顛帝國、印度政府及駐印度英軍；藏方為以拉薩中央政府為核心、各地方部隊共同防守的西藏政府與藏軍。尼泊爾不是交戰國，但尼泊爾出身的廓爾喀士兵隸屬印度軍，隨英方作戰。中國沒有與英軍直接交戰，也未在戰役中派兵馳援拉薩。錫金當時是英屬保護地，充當集結、越境與補給基地，不能誤列為藏方交戰國。
countriesEn: The conflict began in December 1903 when British India crossed the border between Sikkim and Tibet at the Jelep La, and military operations continued into 1904. Its more accurate designation is therefore the First British Expedition to Tibet, 1903–1904. The British belligerent was the British Empire, the Government of India, and British troops stationed in India. The opposing side was the Tibet government centered on Lhasa and the Tibetan forces drawn from different regions. Nepal was not a belligerent, although Gurkha soldiers of Nepali origin served in the Indian Army and fought on the British side. China did not fight British troops directly or send a military relief force to Lhasa during the campaign. Sikkim, then a British protectorate, served as the assembly, transit, and supply base and should not be listed as a Tibetan belligerent.
people: 英方軍事指揮為 Francis Younghusband。他此前曾率領1902年赴拉薩的使團，因未能與藏方達成協議而失敗，1903年則改以武裝遠征迫使拉薩談判。印度總督 Lord Curzon 是推動越境政策的主要政治決策者；印度政府外交秘書 Sir Charles Bell 負責政治指示及談判工作。英軍核心由印度陸軍步兵、廓爾喀營、印度山地部隊及數量較少的英籍步兵組成，另配皇家工兵、醫療、通信和運輸人員。藏方由拉薩中央調兵，各地方首領分別率領所部作戰；江孜宗山守軍依城防部署指揮，並沒有一支完全現代化、統一指揮全藏的野戰部隊。
peopleEn: The British military commander was Francis Younghusband. He had previously led the unsuccessful 1902 mission to Lhasa and, in 1903, returned in command of an armed expedition intended to compel negotiations. Lord Curzon, the Viceroy of India, was the principal political sponsor of the cross-border policy, while Sir Charles Bell, the Foreign Secretary of the Government of India, handled political instructions and negotiations. The combat core consisted of Indian Army infantry, Gurkha units, Indian mountain troops, and a smaller number of British infantry, supported by Royal Engineers, medical, signals, and transport personnel. On the Tibetan side, Lhasa drew troops from the center while regional leaders commanded their own contingents. The garrison at the Gyantse dzong directed the defense locally, and there was no fully modernized field army capable of unified command across Tibet.
kits: 英軍前線步槍為 .303 Lee-Metford Mk I 彈匣槍；此時尚未普遍換用後來定名的 Lee-Enfield。砲兵使用2.5吋7磅速射山砲，這種砲自十九世紀末已在印度軍服役，可拆成適合山地運輸的部件；機槍則為使用 .303 彈藥的 Maxim 機槍。皇家工兵攜帶製式爆破裝置，用於攻破江孜宗山牆體與堡壘。糧秣包括麵粉、罐肉、茶、糖、帳篷、毛毯及鍋具，主要依靠騾子、犛牛和隨軍挑夫運送。藏軍裝備並不一致，主要有長身管火繩槍、少量擊發式前膛槍、進口步槍、刀、矛及少量護甲；江孜守軍另有舊式火砲與火箭，並以宗山地勢構成主要火力支點。
kitsEn: The British front-line rifle was the .303 Lee-Metford Mk I magazine rifle; the Lee-Enfield designation and standard service issue came later. Their artillery included the 2.5-inch 7-pounder quick-firing mountain gun, a weapon already in Indian Army service since the late nineteenth century and capable of being broken into loads suitable for mountain transport. Their machine gun was the .303-caliber Maxim. Royal Engineers carried issued explosive charges for breaching the walls and fortified positions at the Gyantse dzong. Rations and equipment included flour, tinned meat, tea, sugar, tents, blankets, and mess utensils, carried chiefly by mules, yaks, and expedition porters. Tibetan equipment varied by unit, with long-barreled matchlocks, some percussion muzzle-loading firearms, imported rifles, swords, spears, and limited armor. The Gyantse garrison also had old guns and rockets, using the dzong's elevation as its principal firing position.
tactics: 在 Drong 阻斷道路上，英軍先以工兵觀察地形，再讓山砲展開、Maxim 機槍封鎖道路兩側，步兵才以疏散隊形向前推進；砲火削弱藏軍陣地後，英軍才逐步奪取道路。攻打江孜時，英軍沒有立即以密集隊形衝撞城牆，而是先建立包圍、包抄城區外圍及砲兵陣地，工兵在機槍和砲火掩護下把爆破裝置安放於牆體，最後由步兵突擊分隊利用缺口進入宗山。藏軍利用高處射擊，以火繩槍和舊砲延遲接近速度，並利用出擊拖延英軍；外牆被突破後，守軍失去完整射界與相互支援。英軍其後未再強攻拉薩，而是控制政府機關和重要路口，把主要行動轉為談判與條約安排。
tacticsEn: At Drong, British sappers first reconnoitred the blocked road before the mountain guns were unlimbered and Maxim guns covered both flanks. Infantry then advanced in extended formation and took the route only after artillery fire had disrupted the Tibetan positions. At Gyantse, the British did not immediately send dense formations against the walls. They established a blockade, positions around the city, and artillery batteries. Under machine-gun and artillery cover, engineers placed explosive charges in the defenses, after which assault columns entered through the breach. The Tibetan garrison fired from elevated positions, used matchlocks and old guns to delay the attackers, and launched counterattacks. Once the outer wall had been opened and the defenders lost unobstructed firing fields and mutual support, the defense fragmented. The British did not subsequently storm Lhasa; they occupied government offices and key routes and shifted the principal operation toward negotiation and treaty arrangements.
data: 1903年末，主力在錫金 Pedong 一帶集結。1903年12月12日，英軍先頭部隊越過 Jelep La，進入藏境，經 Chumbi Valley，1904年1月初抵達帕里宗，再沿 Tse La 等高地通往江孜。3月28日，英軍在 Drong 與藏軍接戰並打通道路；4月13日開始圍攻江孜，4月17日突破宗山及城區防線。5月17日，英軍進入拉薩；其後數月進行政治談判，9月7日由英藏雙方代表簽訂條約。英方作戰人員約二千，另有數千名隨軍挑夫及大量馱獸。道路大多不能使用車輛，砲身分件由騾子負擔，.303 步槍及機槍彈藥、七磅砲彈藥、口糧和傷藥均靠印度境內總補給站與前進分隊之間的接力運送；傷員也須沿同一條山地道路後送。藏軍死亡總數及英軍作戰傷亡至今沒有完整一致的可核實統計，因此不採用任何未能確定的精確總數。
dataEn: In late 1903, the main force assembled around Pedong in Sikkim. On 12 December 1903, its leading elements crossed the Jelep La into Tibet, moved through the Chumbi Valley, reached Phari Dzong in early January 1904, and then followed the high route past Tse La toward Gyantse. On 28 March, the British fought the Tibetan blocking force at Drong and opened the road. They began the siege of Gyantse on 13 April and broke through the dzong and city defenses on 17 April. The British entered Lhasa on 17 May. Political negotiations followed, and representatives of Britain and Tibet signed a treaty on 7 September. The expedition included approximately two thousand combatants, several thousand porters, and a large number of pack animals. Most of the route could not take wheeled vehicles. Mountain guns were carried in separate loads, while .303 rifle and machine-gun ammunition, 7-pounder ammunition, rations, and medical supplies moved by relay from the main depot in India to the advancing columns. Wounded had to be evacuated over the same difficult route. No complete, consistent, verifiable totals exist for Tibetan military deaths or British combat casualties, so no uncertain numerical total is adopted here.
cause: 戰爭的直接背景是英國與拉薩方面長期談判未能就打開貿易及建立 British trade agents 達成安排。西藏仍與British India進行交易，但對英國商人入境、邊境通行及在江孜設立常駐代表均有嚴格限制；1902年Younghusband使團又未能取得拉薩接受英方要求。Curzon把經濟准入與戰略安全視為同一問題：英國擔心俄羅斯經中亞向西藏擴展影響，也希望確認錐金、不丹及印度北部邊界的安全安排。部分英方官員還希望藉軍事聲望影響拉薩內政及 ninth Panchen Lama 的政治立場。由於英方不承認西藏能完全排除其他外國勢力，最終選擇以遠征施加壓力。此次越境並非由一場大規模邊境襲擊引發，而是印度總督府在外交途徑失敗後作出的政策決定。
causeEn: The immediate background was the failure of prolonged negotiations between Britain and Lhasa over trade access and the establishment of British trade agents. Tibet continued to trade with British India but imposed substantial restrictions on the entry of British merchants, border travel, and a permanent British representative at Gyantse. Younghusband's 1902 mission also failed to obtain Lhasa's acceptance of British demands. Curzon treated commercial access and strategic security as a single problem. Britain was concerned about Russian influence reaching Tibet through Central Asia and also sought to secure its arrangements concerning Sikkim, Bhutan, and the northern frontier of India. Some British officials further hoped that the expedition's military prestige would influence Lhasa's internal politics and the position of the ninth Panchen Lama. Because London did not accept that Tibet could exclude every other outside power, it chose to apply military pressure. The crossing was therefore not the consequence of a major border attack, but a policy decision taken by the Indian administration after the diplomatic route had failed.
impact: Drong與江孜的失敗，使拉薩方面明白英屬印度能以約二千名作戰人員及有限砲兵把軍隊送至拉薩，並迫使藏方在外交上接受英方提出的制度安排。戰後條約使英國得以在江孜設立貿易機構，對拉薩對外關係形成長期限制；藏方為尋求新的安全與外交來源，也開始加強軍隊整編、外國武器購置及後勤體系。清廷也因西藏未能抵擋英軍而加速推動西藏行政與邊防改革，但清廷本身沒有因此同英國開戰。英國取得的是貿易與外交據點，而非對西藏的完整兼併；拉薩政府沒有被推翻，英軍也沒有長期駐紮拉薩。短期內英國削弱了其所認定的俄國影響，長期則留下更深的藏英不信任與軍事對立。
impactEn: The defeats at Drong and Gyantse demonstrated to Lhasa that British India could move roughly two thousand combatants and a small artillery force as far as the Tibetan capital and compel diplomatic acceptance of British arrangements. The subsequent treaty allowed Britain to establish a trade agency at Gyantse and imposed long-term restrictions on Tibet's foreign relations. To seek alternative sources of security and diplomatic support, the Tibetan government subsequently reorganized its army, obtained additional foreign weapons, and improved military logistics. The Qing court also accelerated administrative and frontier reforms in Tibet after discovering that its forces had not been able to stop the British, although China did not enter the war. Britain obtained trading and diplomatic footholds rather than a complete annexation: Lhasa's government was not replaced, and British troops were not permanently stationed there. The immediate effect was to weaken the Russian influence that London perceived in Tibet, but the longer-term result included deeper Tibetan-British mistrust and military confrontation.
result: 軍事結果沒有逆轉：藏軍在 Drong 與江孜失去主動權，英軍占領拉薩的重要機關，並在1904年9月7日簽訂《拉薩條約》。條約規定在江孜、昌都、巴塘、阿墩子及噶爾托克設立貿易市場，由英國派駐貿易代表；藏方支付75,000英鎊賠償款，分五十年償付；涉及對外關係的事項須與英國協商辦理。英藏代表完成簽署後，英方主力分批撤回印度，只在江孜保留貿易代表及有限守軍。英國沒有兼併西藏，也沒有廢除拉薩政府；條約使英國取得具體商業與外交權力，則把西藏置於明顯不對等的國際地位。戰役因此以江孜陷落、拉薩占領及條約簽署作結，而不是以英軍長期駐留或藏方政府被更替作結。
resultEn: The military result was not reversed. Tibetan forces lost the initiative at Drong and Gyantse, British troops occupied key government positions in Lhasa, and the Treaty of Lhasa was signed on 7 September 1904. It provided for trading marts and British trade agents at Gyantse, Chiamdo, Batang, Atuntze, and Gartok. Tibet was required to pay an indemnity of £75,000 over fifty years and to conduct matters concerning foreign relations in concert with Britain. After the signing, the main British expeditionary force withdrew to India in stages, leaving a trade agent and a limited guard at Gyantse. Britain did not annex Tibet or abolish the Lhasa government. The treaty secured concrete commercial and diplomatic rights while placing Tibet in a markedly unequal international position. The campaign therefore ended with the fall of Gyantse, the occupation of Lhasa, and the signed treaty, rather than with a permanent British military occupation or the replacement of the Tibetan government.
